minor.issue: One generic sentence; omits sample (27 studies, 617 athletes), meta-analytic results and the authors' caution about low study quality.
States no effect on objective sleep measures without noting objective onset latency became significant after removing a heterogeneous study (g=0.81) and that subjective sleep duration was unaffected.
Omits non-pre-registered protocol, only 2/22 studies with power analysis, poor blinding/concealment, no RCTs of sleep extension, under-representation of females and absence of para-athletes.

'Start with individualized behavioral and environmental sleep support' goes beyond the authors, who say they are 'hesitant to provide applied recommendations' and only propose testing tailored strategies.
Medication-use advice is not a finding of the review (medication appears only in background); framed as if supported.
Generic RTP statement; does not state that the review did not study injured athletes or return to sport.
Could note that sleep-quality effect became non-significant when semi-elite trials were removed (g=0.38, CI -0.11 to 0.90), relevant to elite populations.

note: Both are accurate on the pooled effects, but B is complete and well-caveated (onset-latency sensitivity, quality limits, no RTP data) while A is thin and adds practice advice the authors explicitly declined to give.
